subject: science
notes: Each year, winds carry millions of tons of dust from the Sahara across the Atlantic Ocean.
Much of the dust comes from the Bodélé Depression, a dry lakebed in Chad.
Some of the dust settles on the Amazon rainforest in South America.
The dust contains phosphorus, a nutrient that plants need to grow.
Heavy rains continually wash phosphorus out of the Amazon's soils.
Scientists estimate that the phosphorus delivered in Saharan dust roughly makes up for the amount lost.
stem: The student wants to explain why the Amazon rainforest needs phosphorus from elsewhere and how Saharan dust supplies it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Saharan dust that settles on the Amazon contains phosphorus, a nutrient plants need, in roughly the amount the rainforest loses.
choices.B: Because heavy rains wash phosphorus from Amazon soils, the rainforest relies on wind-borne Saharan dust to bring in the nutrient.
choices.C: Each year, winds carry millions of tons of dust from the Sahara, much of it from a dry lakebed in Chad, across the Atlantic Ocean.
choices.D: Heavy rains in the Amazon continually wash phosphorus, a nutrient that plants need in order to grow, out of the rainforest's soils.

explanation.why: The goal has two parts: why the Amazon needs outside phosphorus (rain washes it from the soil) and how the Sahara supplies it (wind-borne dust carries it). Only one choice links the cause of the shortage to the source of the supply.
explanation.A: Incorrect. It explains how the dust supplies phosphorus but not why the Amazon needs it from elsewhere; "the amount the rainforest loses" is mentioned without saying how it is lost. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.B: Correct. It explains the shortage (rain washes phosphorus away) and the remedy (Saharan dust brings it in).
explanation.C: Incorrect. It describes the dust's journey but does not mention phosphorus or why the Amazon needs it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. It explains why phosphorus is lost but never mentions Saharan dust.
